scope: Corollary 2.3 (Dyadic junta approximation) of the manuscript “Constant-factor hardness of directed feedback vertex set” (preprints/Constant-factor-hardness-of-directed-feedback-vertex-set-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 102 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 606657a956af61c2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let p = 2−k, where k ≥ 1 is an integer. For every b ≥ 0 and α > 0, there is a finite integer J(p, b, α), independent of |S|, such that every Boolean function f : 2S → {0, 1} with Ip(f) ≤ b has a Boolean junta approximant on at most J(p, b, α) coordinates with error at most α under µS p .
